name: Sheffield Support Group
description: About our group You can read the latest newsletter here. If you would like adding to the mailing list please call Val Heap on 0114 262 0468 or email [email protected]. You can also find us on Facebook, here. The ethos of the Sheffield Support Group is to support activities to enable people with Parkinson’s to build physical and mental wellness through participation in social events, learning and creative activities with like-minded people. The group is run for the charity by volunteers who are living with Parkinson’s themselves, or who have experience of Parkinson’s. It is supported by professional staff to: Offer information, friendship, and support to those with Parkinson’s, their carers, families and friends Organise or assist with events and social activities for members Raise funds for research to support people affected by Parkinson’s We believe that doing something positive for yourself is good for the soul. We arrange classes and activities that include: Posture and general fitness, Boxing, Pilates, Tango, Voice (singing), Saturday morning walks and monthly meetings, with a speaker, and an opportunity to meet others over a cup of tea A monthly drop in Parkinson’s Cafe held in Parson Cross Community Development Forum "A Positively Parkinson’s" group that holds monthly evening socials at the Waggon and Horses restaurant/pub on Abbeydale Road and is aimed at people aged 66 years and under A Supporters Group for those living with a person with Parkinson's We also signpost to privately run classes and other resources that may be of interest to people affected by Parkinson’s in the Sheffield area, eg: PD Warrior programme Personalised strength and fitness A machine-based circuits class We follow the values of Parkinson’s UK by putting People first and at the centre of decisions, Uniting all those who are affected by Parkinson’s in Sheffield, Pioneering with a can-do attitude and we are Driven to find a cure and offer support until one is found. Volunteers needed! We need to recruit volunteers to help us run the group. Do you have an hour or two per month to spare? If so we would be delighted to hear from you. For more information please email [email protected].
address: Tapton Masonic Hall, Shore Lane Sheffield, Sheffield, S10 3BU

name: Horsham and District Branch
description: For more information about our group, contact us or visit our website: https://horsham.parkinsonsuk.group/ Our local group offers friendship and support to people with Parkinson’s, their families, and carers. For information and advice on Parkinson’s, or emotional support, call the Parkinson’s UK helpline on 0808 800 0303. Our branch organizes various popular activities four days a week, almost every week of the year. We believe that keeping moving is crucial in Parkinson’s to slow its progression and enhance overall quality of life. It’s essential to find activities that suit your interests, are enjoyable, and supervised by specialists in the specific activity to maximize benefits and minimize the risk of injury. We’ve categorized our activities into three intensity levels: high, medium, and low. For more details, visit our website. Each activity is associated with a contact point. We provide information and timings for these activities, and we also have an online calendar to keep you updated on what’s happening. We recognise the importance of socialisation and problem-solving for individuals with Parkinson’s. We offer two types of meetings: a branch meeting where we invite speakers to discuss various topics, and a working-age group social meeting held in a pub. This latter meeting provides a more informal setting for confidential conversations with other Parkinson’s-affected individuals. For more information, visit our website. Our branch is supported by a team of friendly volunteers, but we always welcome others who would like to contribute. In addition to our local activities, we fundraise to support local activities, research, Parkinson’s nurses, and other services. If you’re interested in helping, please get in touch.

description: Our aim is to provide a UK wide place of support to discuss the unique challenges of being a service person, family member of a service person or a veteran with Parkinson's. scheduleText: Get in touch for more information.

name: Online Working Age / Newly Diagnosed Carers Support Group
description: The group is open to all carers and family members aged over 18 and under 67 supporting someone newly diagnosed with Parkinson’s. You do not have to be a registered carer. It's free to join. The informal online sessions are facilitated by volunteers with caring experience and a chance to talk with people in similar situations, share experiences, and support each other. We aim for the group to provide mutual support to those living with or caring for a person diagnosed with Parkinson’s within (approximately) the last 3 years. If you do not meet the newly diagnosed or age criteria, we host another online carers support group, which you are welcome to join. For carers under the age of 18, we suggest finding a group specifically aimed for young carers would best meet your needs. This online group is for peer-to-peer support and is not monitored by professional advisers. If participants want additional or one-to-one support, they may be signposted by volunteers to other groups, services, or other Parkinson’s UK support opportunities. Places are limited to 15 to help ensure people feel supported and listened to. The group is closed and we plan to only take new participants if space becomes available after the first six sessions. This is to allow the group to build trusting relationships with the same people. If the group becomes oversubscribed, a waiting list will be created for people wanting to join the next six sessions. Join our session on the 3rd Wednesday of the month, from 7pm to 8.30pm. To book a place, please contact Satpal using the contact details below. When booking, please provide your name, email address, telephone number, and address.
scheduleText: Monthly on the third Wednesday From 19:00 until 20:30
